Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme. A big ph site <TEXTITOPEN_0001><MATH_0002><TEXTITCLOSE_0001>
is any site constructed as follows:
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> Choose a big ph site <MATH_0003> as in
Topologies, Section <REF_0001>.
<STRUCT_0003> As underlying category take the category <MATH_0004>
of algebraic spaces over <MATH_0005> (see discussion in
Section <REF_0002> why this is a set).
<STRUCT_0004> Choose any set of coverings as in
Sets, Lemma <REF_0003> starting with the
category <MATH_0006> and the class of ph coverings
of Definition <REF_0004>.
<STRUCT_0005>

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme. Let <MATH_0002> be as in
Definition <REF_0001>.
Let <MATH_0003> be an algebraic space over <MATH_0004>, i.e., an object of
<MATH_0005>. Then the big ph site
<TEXTITOPEN_0001><MATH_0006><TEXTITCLOSE_0001> of <MATH_0007>
is the localization of the site <MATH_0008>
at <MATH_0009> introduced in Sites, Section <REF_0002>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme. Let <MATH_0002> be an algebraic space over <MATH_0003>.
Let <MATH_0004> be a presheaf on <MATH_0005>.
Then <MATH_0006> is a sheaf if and only if
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0007> satisfies the sheaf condition for <ACCENT_0001>tale coverings, and
<STRUCT_0003> if <MATH_0008> is a proper surjective morphism of
<MATH_0009>, then
<MATH_0010> maps bijectively to the equalizer
of the two maps <MATH_0011>.
<STRUCT_0004>

We will show that if (1) and (2) hold, then <MATH_0001> is sheaf.
Let <MATH_0002> be a ph covering, i.e., a covering in
<MATH_0003>.
We will verify the sheaf condition for this covering.
Let <MATH_0004> be sections which restrict to the same
section over <MATH_0005>. We will show that there exists a
unique section <MATH_0006> restricting to <MATH_0007> over <MATH_0008>.
Let <MATH_0009> be an <ACCENT_0001>tale covering with <MATH_0010> affine.
By property (1) it suffices to produce sections <MATH_0011>
which agree on <MATH_0012> in order to produce <MATH_0013>.
Consider the ph coverings <MATH_0014>.
Then <MATH_0015> are sections agreeing
over <MATH_0016>.
Choose a proper surjective morphism <MATH_0017> and a finite affine
open covering <MATH_0018> such that the standard ph covering
<MATH_0019> refines <MATH_0020>.
If <MATH_0021>
denotes the pullback of <MATH_0022> to <MATH_0023> by the
implied morphisms, then we find that <MATH_0024> glue to a section
<MATH_0025>. Using the agreement on overlaps
once more, we find that <MATH_0026> is in the equalizer of the two
maps <MATH_0027>.
Hence by (2) we find that <MATH_0028> comes from a unique section
<MATH_0029>. We omit the verification that these
sections <MATH_0030> have all the desired properties.
